analytic.title: Towards a Schedulable Fault Tolerant HW-SW Mapping for Real Time Systems

div.p: An important part in the design of real-time systems is the allocation and scheduling of the software tasks onto the hardware architecture. This faces the challenge of meeting deadlines, completion times, earliest start times and tolerating faults. Unfortunately, these processes are far from trivial due to the wide range of complex constraints that typically appear in real-time systems. The lack of edibility and expressive power in existing scheduling frameworks makes it difficult to model the system accurately. Moreover, the designed system must be cost-effective in terms of resource utilization which implies the need for an optimization approach. In order to tackle these deficiencies this paper proposes a schedulable faulttolerant hardware-software mapping methodology for real time systems.The design optimization approach decides the mapping of jobs to nodes such that the timing constraints of the application are satisfied. Experimental studies show that the proposed method outperforms existing dominant work.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Real-time systems are playing a crucial role in our society, and in the last two decades, there has been an explosive growth in the number of real-time systems being used in our daily lives and in industrial production. Systems such as nuclear plant control, space missions, flight control systems, anti-missile technology and so on all make use of real-time technologies. The most important attribute of real-time systems is that the correctness of such systems depends not only on the computed results but also on the time at which results are produced. Schedulability analysis enables these guarantees to be provided. In scheduling theory, a real-time system comprises a set of real-time tasks; each task consists of an infinite or finite stream of jobs. The task set can be scheduled by a number of policies including fixed priority or dynamic priority algorithms. The success of a real-time system depends on whether all the jobs of all the tasks can be guaranteed to complete their executions before their deadlines [1], [2].

Due to the critical nature of tasks in a real-time system, it is essential that every task admitted in the system completes its execution even in the presence of faults. Therefore, fault-tolerance is an important requirement in such systems. Scheduling multiple versions of tasks on different processors can provide faulttolerance [3], [4].Applying the fault tolerant scheme in real time scheduling make it more challenging to map the software jobs into hardware nodes.Fault-tolerance is an important requirement in embedded systems which interact with a dynamic environment in safety-critical applications. In safety-critical real-time systems, missing the deadline of a task can pose threat to human lives. Moreover, when faults occur in such system, recovery from the error before deadline of a job is must.

The main problem of allocating tasks to processing nodes in a real time system is maintaining various timing constraints and ensuring the fault tolerance. The lack of expressive power in the existing fault tolerant mapping algorithms makes it very difficult to model the system efficiently. The correct scheduling decisions along with the fault tolerant scheme have to make within a short period of time and limited resources. This paper proposes a new and efficient fault-tolerant job scheduling among hardware nodes. The fault tolerance is adopted by replicating jobs. The number of replication depends on the system complexity which is measured by summing the complexity of the program and the number of variable dependency of the program. According to the complexity of the jobs, replicated jobs are assigned to different nodes. This paper has two goals (I) assigning jobs onto suitable HW nodes such that FT requirements are met (Replica scheduling) and (II) ordering job executions in time (scheduling). The experimental studies prove that the proposed method reduces the search space and finds a quick feasible solution for the mapping. The paper is organized as follows. Section 2 depicts the related work. The proposed methodology is described in Section 3. Section 4 provides the experimental setup and analysis. The paper concludes in Section 5 and recommends for future extensions.

div.head: II. RELATED WORK
div.p: Liestman and Campbell [6] proposed a set of scheduling algorithms for fault tolerant real-time systems. This method involves three algorithms. First algorithm creates an optimal schedule for a time interval equal to the maximum period among jobs. Second algorithm reschedules remaining jobs in a partial schedule if a primary succeeds. The problem in this methodology is second algorithm is computationally expensive, since it calls for redoing the schedule upon completion of the primary. In a real time system it will not give the feasible and efficient solution. Constraints prioritization is applied in [7] during the allocation phase in order to satisfy the constraints which also reduce the complexity to solve the problem. [8] Specifically addresses the dependability driven mapping (focuses on minimizing interaction) and presents the heuristics for doing the mapping. A survey of various SW development processes addressing dependability as extra-functional requirements at both late and early phases is described in [9]. Utilizing model-based principle, Yin et. al. [10] describes a component integration method for designing and deploying avionics systems. Krishna and Shin shows [11] the problem of preventing processor failures by keeping backup schedules. They assumed the existence of an algorithm, which allocates and schedules jobs on the nodes so that all the tasks meet their deadline. Their aim was to obtain an efficient algorithm to generate fault tolerant schedules for tolerating node failures. Ramos-Thuel and Strosnider [12] presented a new algorithm called time reservation algorithm that reserves time for fault recovery modules. Ghoshet. al [13] presented a method for guaranteeing that the real-time tasks will meet the deadlines under transient faults, by resorting to reserving sufficient slack in queue-based schedules. But in real time system, it is not efficient. Sharif et. al [14] proposed a methodology that maps the software components (jobs) into hardware nodes. In this paper, the jobs are ordered and hence give an efficient result. But the main problem of their work is, they do not order the nodes.

div.head: III. THE PROPOSED METHODOLOGY OF HARDWARE-SOFTWARE MAPPING
div.p: This paper presents a fault tolerant scheduling policy so that the jobs are distributed to processing nodes efficiently. Let an event denote a task arrival, departure or discarding. In order to be acceptable in the context described in this paper, a scheduling policy is assumed to preserve the sorting of jobs according to their execution priority between consecutive events (the priorities are allowed to change in time, but the sorting of tasks according to their priorities is allowed to change only at event times). All practically used priority based scheduling policies. The priority of a job is determined by deadlines, earliest start time, computation time, complexity of the job.

The proposed methodology considers both nodes and jobs ordering. It enables to find the correct nodes fora job and thus gives a feasible optimal solution. From the computation time (CT) and earliest start time (EST) of each segment relative to the beginning of the process containing that segment, the computation time, and deadline of each job, one should be able to compute the release time, computation time, and the deadline for each segment.The proposed methodology finds a valid feasible schedule in which all jobs completes their computation before their deadlines. The methodology will terminate as soon as it finds a feasible schedule that meets all deadline constraints. If the original problem is non-feasible, i.e., no feasible schedule exists that can satisfy all constraints, the algorithm will also terminate as soon as it determines the case. There may have some jobs that do not have any scheduling. In this case, the specific non-schedulable jobs are printed out. The steps of the methodology are outlined briefly as follows STEP 1: Determine the complexity of a job. STEP 7: Sort the processing node according to their speed, availability or reliability. Here it is assumed that the processing nodes are by default in an ordered fashion.

div.head: A. Measuring the Complexity of the Jobs
div.p: Job complexity is the summation of the variable dependency and the time complexity of the code. First, it has to compute the number of dependable variables. Then the time complexity of the job has to be measured. Figure 1 presents an example of complexity of a job. In the sample program in Figure 1, the for loop continues 45 times and there is only one statement inside the loop. There is another line that must execute before the above for loop. Therefore, total number of lines executed in the program (job) is 1+(45*1)=46.
Variable dependency is 1 in the program. Hence the total job complexity of the code is 46+1=47.

Figure 2 shows the measurement of complexity of the program in Figure 1. Example program 3 have a variable dependency of 68. Variable b is dependent to variables c and j. For this reason here variable dependency is 2. Variable 'a' is dependent to variables 'a', 'b' and 'c'. The total number of dependency is hence 5.

For the hw-sw mapping, all the defined constraints are to be satisfied. First, the job list has to be ordered (Step 3 in algorithm 2). If all the constraints are hold (Step 6 in algorithm 2), i.e., consistency enforcing is ensured, then the job is selected for the first node.If the constraints do not hold for the current node, then selects the next node. It is assumed that, the nodes are ordered. If no solution is found, then backtrack (Step 8 in algorithm 2). If no feasible solution is found, then report the mapping is unfeasible. div.head: IV. EXPERIMENTAL SETUP AND PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS
div.p: In order to evaluate the proposed methodology, it needs to depict the experimental setup. Different set of jobs from 5 to 20 are randomly selected and denoted as J1, J2…., Jn. The job properties are selected randomly within the following ranges and are given in Table III. Replica number depends on the complexity of the job. The HW model comprises of varied number for nodes (from 2 to 10). In order to demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach, here provides illustrations of different scenarios.

Several experiments have been carried out to evaluate the performance of the scheduling heuristics. Assume that, there are two processing nodes n1 and n2, three jobs j1, j2, j3 in a real time system and processor n1 is more reliable, available and faster than the processing node n2. It has to be scheduled so that it maintains the constraints given in the table below. Figure 8 shows the total solution space of the given problem. After applying the constraints, the solution space is reduced and finally there are two acceptable solutions. The two acceptable solutions are (i) Job J1 and J3 are assigned to node n1 and J2 is assigned to node n2 i.e., n1= {J1, J3} and n2= {J2} and (ii) Job J1 and J3 are assigned to node n2 and J2 is assigned to node n1 i.e., n1= {J2} and n2= {J1, J3}. As the proposed algorithm has a node ordering heuristic and on the basis of this heuristic, processing node n1 is more effective than the processing node n2, hence the first solution is the optimal solution. Computation time is the time needed for run the code. It can easily represented by the number of iteration. For the same number of jobs, the number of iteration for the proposed methodology and existing methodology Sharif et. al. [14] is compared in Figure 9. It can be observed from Figure 9 that for the same number of jobs, the proposed method requires fewer iterations than Sharif et. al. [14].

div.head: IV. CONCLUSIONS
div.p: In this paper, a methodology of schedulability driven hardware-software mapping for the real time system is proposed addressing the problem of scheduling and fault tolerance in real-time systems. The proposed new methodology of mapping based on schedulability analysis enables to manage a wide range of constraints. It is emphasized more on the efficiency of the methodology as it works with real time system. Some extra-functional requirements have been considered to reduce the design efforts and costs. The comprehensive mapping strategy ensures the best schedulability analysis. Experimental results show the effectiveness, performance of our design process as it considers the important aspects: (i) uses of job and node ordering heuristics, (ii) checking the constraints during the assignment process which reduces the search space. The results indicate that the methodology indeed has the potential of becoming a valuable tool in the system design process of real time system. From a research perspective, perhaps the concern is how to improve various aspects of the scheduling problem. The proposed methodology does this by job and node ordering heuristics. An extension to the hardware architecture would be the possibility to have multiple busses that each connects a cluster of nodes. This is often the case where the entire system is divided into sub-systems that have different performance and reliability requirements.
